body:
Adityaram Vyas

Adityaram Vyas (1819-1880) was an important early Gujarati classical musician, composer and teacher. He was born in Junagadh and later became a royal musician in Jamnagar.

He received musical training from his father and subsequently studied under Ustad Nannumiya. He developed expertise in Hindustani classical music and contributed particularly to the preservation and teaching of dhrupad.

His important musical work, Sangitaditya, contains compositions associated with his musical tradition.

His career demonstrates that royal support for classical music in Gujarat was not confined to Baroda. Other princely states, including Junagadh and Jamnagar, also provided opportunities for musicians to develop and transmit their knowledge.

Pandit Omkarnath Thakur

Pandit Omkarnath Thakur (1897-1967) was a distinguished Hindustani classical vocalist, musicologist and educator from Gujarat.

He received musical training from Pandit Vishnu Digambar Paluskar, an important figure in the institutional development of Indian classical music education.

Omkarnath Thakur was a representative of the Gwalior gharana. He became the first dean of the music and fine arts institution known as Kala-Sangeet-Bharati at Banaras Hindu University.

His important musical writings include:

  • Sangeetanjali
  • Pranava Bharati

He contributed to classical music both as a performer and as an educator. His Gujarat connection should be distinguished from his professional work at Banaras Hindu University.

Ustad Maula Bakhsh

Ustad Maula Bakhsh was an important musician and music educator associated with the Baroda court. Under the patronage of Sayajirao Gaekwad III, he became the founder-principal of the Gayan Shala established in 1886.

His principal historical significance lies in the development of organised music education in Baroda.

Ustad Abdul Karim Khan

Ustad Abdul Karim Khan (1872-1937) was a prominent Hindustani classical vocalist and a leading figure in the development of the Kirana gharana.

He served as a court musician in Baroda and subsequently contributed to the spread of the Kirana tradition in other parts of India.

His association with the Baroda court is shared with Faiyaz Khan, but their gharanas are different.

Dahyabhai Shivram Naik and other musical contributions

Gujarat's musical literature also includes Sangeet Kaladhar, associated with the musicologist Dahyalal Shivram Naik. His given name is also rendered as Dahyabhai in some references.

Works such as Sangeet Kaladhar and Adityaram Vyas's Sangitaditya represent efforts to preserve and communicate musical knowledge through written literature.

Rahim Khan is also remembered in accounts of Gujarat's musical heritage as a musician associated with the been, a traditional Indian string instrument in this classical music context.

Faculty of Performing Arts, Maharaja Sayajirao University

The Faculty of Performing Arts of the Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda is an important institutional successor to the music school established under Sayajirao Gaekwad III.

The original Gayan Shala was founded in February 1886 with Maula Bakhsh as its founder-principal. It gradually developed into an institution providing formal education in Indian classical music and other performing arts.

Institutional development

  • 1886: Establishment of Gayan Shala in Baroda.
  • 1916: First All-India Music Conference, led by Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande under royal patronage.
  • 1949: Establishment of the Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda.
  • 1950: Introduction of degree-level music education in the university's music department.
  • 1984: The institution received separate faculty status as the Faculty of Performing Arts.

As of 25 November 2026, the university's official faculty profile identifies departments covering vocal music, instrumental music, tabla, dance and dramatics.

Gujarat Rajya Sangeet Natak Akademi

The Gujarat Rajya Sangeet Natak Akademi, also called the Gujarat State Sangeet Natak Akademi, promotes the performing arts of Gujarat.

The institution received autonomous Akademi status from the state government on 1 September 1992. Its activities extend beyond classical music to include dance, theatre and folk arts.

Its music-related activities include:

  • Tana-Riri classical music programmes.
  • Classical music concerts and competitions commemorating Pandit Omkarnath Thakur.
  • Opportunities for young musicians to perform.
  • Musical training programmes and recognition of artistic achievements.

The Gujarat State Sangeet Natak Akademi is a state-level institution for performing arts. It should not be confused with the national Sangeet Natak Akademi or institutions concerned primarily with literature and visual arts.

Saptak School of Music and the Saptak Festival

Saptak is an important classical music initiative based in Ahmedabad. Its annual music festival began in 1980.

The initiative was developed by musicians and music enthusiasts, including tabla player Nandan Mehta and sitarist Manju Mehta.

Saptak combines musical education with public performances. Its annual festival provides opportunities for established classical musicians and emerging artists to perform before audiences.

Tana-Riri Mahotsav

The Tana-Riri Mahotsav is associated with Vadnagar. It commemorates the legendary singer sisters Tana and Riri and celebrates Gujarat's classical music heritage.

The festival has been held annually at Vadnagar since 2003 and is associated with the Gujarat State Sangeet Natak Akademi. Its commemorative purpose distinguishes it from Saptak, which developed as an educational and musical initiative in Ahmedabad.
